result.description: Copper is a CRM built around Google Workspace. It manages contacts, companies, leads, opportunities, projects, tasks and activities.
result.auth_detail: Per-user API key sent in headers (X-PW-AccessToken plus the user's email), generated in System settings > API Keys. OAuth2.0 is described as the preferred approach for partner integrations. The OAuth doc pages gave no readable text, so I could not confirm how OAuth client credentials are obtained.
result.access_detail: Each end user can generate their own API key in their Copper account, with no app review or listing. This is not a gate under audit rule 1. Copper has no free tier. It offers a trial ("Start free, no credit card required") and then paid plans from $23-29 per seat per month, so a Copper account is needed. The pricing page does not say API access is limited to higher plans. The developer docs did not mention a plan restriction or a developer sandbox. OAuth for multi-tenant apps may need partner onboarding with Copper. That is unverified, because the OAuth pages did not render text.
result.api_notes: The REST Developer API covers account/users, leads, people, companies, opportunities, projects, tasks, activities, custom fields, pipelines, webhooks and related items. It has search endpoints and bulk endpoints. The rate limit is 180 requests per minute, with an extra 3 requests per second on bulk APIs.
result.blocker: Credentials need a paid or trial Copper account, with no free tier. Per-user API keys work for self-serve. OAuth for multi-tenant use may need partner arrangement with Copper, which I could not confirm. No official MCP server found.

evidence.quote: There are two ways to access the Copper Developer API: API keys and OAuth2.0 .
API Keys are suitable for individual users, while OAuth2.0 is the preferred approach for partner integrations.
To generate an API token, in the Copper web app go to System settings > API Keys and click the 'GENERATE API KEY'
Start free, no credit card required.
All API calls are limited to 180 requests per minute.
MCP server for Copper CRM: let Claude, Cursor and other AI agents search contacts and deals, review the pipeline, and log notes and tasks. Unofficial.
